reviewMethod: Antigravity drafts separately reviewed against complete archived version bodies and source notes; source discrepancies retained explicitly.

headings.title: Discretionary direction for pretrial conference of attorneys
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the court to direct attorneys to appear for a pretrial conference to consider issue simplification, amendments, admissions, and expert limits.

headings.title: Pretrial order reciting conference agreements and limiting trial issues
headings.reviewNote: Requires the court to enter a pretrial order reciting action taken and agreements reached, which governs subsequent proceedings unless modified.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections on discretionary pretrial conferences of attorneys, binding pretrial orders, and pretrial calendars.

headings.title: Service of written interrogatories on adverse parties
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes any party to serve written interrogatories upon adverse parties, to be answered by the party or designated organizational officer.

headings.title: Time and manner of answering interrogatories under oath
headings.reviewNote: Requires written answers under oath signed by the answering person and served within fifteen days after delivery unless the court enlarges or shortens the time.

headings.title: Time for presenting objections to interrogatories
headings.reviewNote: Requires objections to interrogatories to be filed within ten days of service, deferring answers until the court resolves objections.

headings.title: Single set limitation on interrogatories without court leave
headings.reviewNote: Restricts parties from serving more than one set of interrogatories to the same party absent leave of court.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections on interrogatories; corrected subsection 2 note from 30 days to statutory 15-day answer period.

headings.title: Motion and good cause for production and inspection of documents and tangibles
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes court orders on motion showing good cause to produce non-privileged documents/tangibles (*"or" for "of" in original rolls) or permit property entry for inspection.

headings.title: Party entitlement to copies of own previously made statements
headings.reviewNote: Allows a party to obtain copies of their own previously made statements without showing good cause, defining qualifying statements.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections and original-rolls footnote (*"or" for "of") on document/property inspection orders and party entitlement to prior own statements.

headings.title: Prohibition on disclosing recordings and photographs of minor sexual offense victims
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits copying or distributing recordings or photographs of minor victims of chapter 566 offenses without a court order.

headings.title: Authorized multidisciplinary access and investigatory sharing
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes access and sharing of recordings/photographs by multidisciplinary team members, DSS, DMH, office of child advocate, child abuse and neglect review board, and attorney general.

headings.title: Mandatory protective provisions in judicial disclosure orders
headings.reviewNote: Prescribes protective terms for court disclosure orders, restricting use to trial preparation and prohibiting unauthorized dissemination.

headings.title: Multidisciplinary discretion to permit viewing without reproduction
headings.reviewNote: Preserves multidisciplinary team discretion to allow in-person viewing of materials without permitting reproduction or copying.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections on minor sexual offense recordings/photographs; removed extratextual "defense counsel" from subsection 2 authorized-sharing list.

headings.title: Written request for admission of document genuineness and relevant facts
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes written requests for admission of document genuineness or truth of relevant matters after pleadings are closed.

headings.title: Limitation of admissions strictly to pending action
headings.reviewNote: Restricts the effect of admissions solely to the pending action, prohibiting their use in any other proceeding.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections on written requests for admission of document genuineness/facts and restriction of admissions to the pending action.

headings.title: Motion to compel answer upon party refusal
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes motions to compel interrogatory answers, requiring payment of court costs incurred in obtaining or opposing the order when refusal or motion lacked substantial justification.

headings.title: Judicial sanctions for noncompliance with discovery orders
headings.reviewNote: Empowers courts to impose just sanctions for disobeying discovery orders, including taking facts as established, precluding claims/defenses/evidence, striking pleadings, staying, dismissing, or default.

headings.title: Court costs for unjustified denial of document genuineness
headings.reviewNote: Requires ordering payment of court costs incurred in proving document genuineness or related facts after sworn denial unless good reasons existed or admissions lacked substantial importance.

headings.title: Sanctions for willful failure to attend deposition or answer interrogatories
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes striking pleadings, dismissing actions, or entering default judgment against a party willfully failing to attend depositions or answer interrogatories.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections and Dickey (553 S.W.2d 518) annotation; removed extratextual "attorney fees" from subsections 1 and 3 (title and notes) and "contempt" from subsection 2 note.

headings.title: Automatic legislative stay during regular and active sessions
headings.reviewNote: Establishes an automatic stay of administrative and court proceedings from January 1 to June 1 or whenever the General Assembly is in session.

headings.title: Proceedings and discovery covered by legislative stay
headings.reviewNote: Extends the legislative stay to all trials, motions, hearings, discovery responses, depositions, and trial court proceedings.

headings.title: Exceptions to legislative stay upon waiver or emergency relief
headings.reviewNote: Exempts proceedings from the legislative stay upon written member waiver, in chapter 288 proceedings, in injunctive relief requests, or where the member faces felony or class A misdemeanor charges.

headings.title: Appellate jurisdiction over termination or modification of legislative stay
headings.reviewNote: Confers original jurisdiction on the court of appeals over applications to terminate or modify a legislative stay.

headings.title: Mandatory continuances during special, veto, and interim committee sessions
headings.reviewNote: Mandates court continuances when legislator counsel or parties attend special sessions, veto sessions, or interim legislative committees.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 5 subsections on automatic legislative stays, scope, exceptions (corrected subsection 3 note to match chapter 288, injunctive relief, and felony/class A misdemeanor), appellate review, and continuances.

headings.title: Mandatory stay of inmate civil action pending grievance resolution
headings.reviewNote: Mandates stay of civil actions brought by incarcerated offenders until grievance resolution systems are fully utilized.

headings.title: Department of corrections offender grievance resolution system
headings.reviewNote: Directs the Department of Corrections to maintain offender grievance systems and lists permissive features (reply time limits, emergency priority, anti-reprisal safeguards, independent review).

headings.title: Precedence of federal statutes governing federal claims
headings.reviewNote: Provides that federal statutes governing federal causes of action control over state inmate grievance stay provisions.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 3 subsections on inmate civil action stays pending grievance exhaustion; removed extratextual 180-day stay limit from subsection 2 title and note.

headings.title: Voluntary dismissal without prejudice before final submission
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes plaintiffs to dismiss actions without prejudice at any time before final submission, prohibiting voluntary dismissal thereafter.

headings.title: Single new trial or appeal after dismissal on adverse ruling
headings.reviewNote: Limits a party granted a dismissal at their request after an adverse ruling preventing recovery to at most one new trial or one appeal as of right challenging that ruling.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections and Stubblefield (485 S.W.2d 126) annotation; corrected subsection 2 title to reflect voluntary dismissal at party request after adverse ruling and one-appeal limit.

headings.title: Consolidation of suits founded upon liquidated demands
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes court consolidation of multiple pending actions on liquidated demands between the same parties to avoid unnecessary costs.

headings.title: Separate trials of claims or issues to avoid prejudice
headings.reviewNote: Empowers courts to order separate trials of any claims, cross-claims, counterclaims, or separate issues in furtherance of convenience or to avoid prejudice.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections on consolidation of suits on liquidated demands and separate trials of claims or issues.

headings.title: Preservation of constitutional right to jury trial
headings.reviewNote: Preserves the constitutional right to jury trial inviolate, specifically including validity of releases and discharges.

headings.title: Methods of waiving trial by jury
headings.reviewNote: Specifies four statutory methods of waiving jury trial: failure to appear, written consent filed with clerk, oral consent entered on minutes, or entering bench trial without objection.

headings.title: Jury trial by party consent in actions against the state
headings.reviewNote: Permits the court, with consent of both parties in nonjury statutory actions against the state, to order a jury trial with the same effect as if of right.

headings.title: Jury trial waiver on behalf of minor or incapacitated person
headings.reviewNote: Provides that where a minor or mentally incapacitated party is represented by a legal representative, jury trial is deemed waived under the four circumstances in subsection 2.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections and Randolph/Attebery annotations; corrected subsection 2 note (four waiver methods), subsection 3 title (removed "advisory"), and subsection 4 note.

headings.title: Clear and convincing standard for intentional harm or flagrant disregard
headings.reviewNote: Bars punitive damages unless the claimant proves by clear and convincing evidence intentional harm without just cause or deliberate and flagrant disregard for others' safety.

headings.title: Requirement of compensatory award exceeding nominal damages
headings.reviewNote: Limits punitive recovery to cases with compensatory awards exceeding nominal damages, except for privacy, property, or constitutional claims.

headings.title: Standards for vicarious punitive liability of employers and principals
headings.reviewNote: Delineates strict conditions for holding employers or principals liable for punitive damages based on acts of agents.

headings.title: Limited employment records discovery upon employer admission of liability
headings.reviewNote: Restricts discovery to employment records when an employer admits liability for an agent's conduct in a compensatory damages claim.

headings.title: Prohibition of punitive claims in initial pleadings and leave requirement
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits punitive damage claims in initial pleadings and establishes procedures for seeking court leave to amend based on supporting evidence.

headings.title: Prohibition on calculating punitive damages based on nonparty harm
headings.reviewNote: Explicitly bars basing punitive damages awards on harm caused to persons who are not parties to the litigation.

headings.title: Prohibition of judgments violating statutory punitive restrictions
headings.reviewNote: Bars entry of any judgment containing punitive damage awards that violate the restrictions and standards of the section.

headings.title: Preservation of consistent common law and statutory punitive limitations
headings.reviewNote: Preserves existing common law limitations and other statutory caps on punitive damages to the extent consistent with the section.

headings.title: Definition of punitive damage award
headings.reviewNote: Defines punitive damage award to include punitive damages, exemplary damages, and awards for aggravating circumstances.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 9 subsections and section 510.262 cross-reference; aligned subsection 1 title/note to statutory "intentional harm" or "deliberate and flagrant disregard" wording.

headings.title: Mandatory bifurcated trial on punitive damages upon party request
headings.reviewNote: Requires bifurcated trials before the same jury on punitive damages issues in all jury actions upon request of any party.

headings.title: First stage determination of compensatory damages and punitive liability
headings.reviewNote: Governs first stage proceedings to determine compensatory liability, damages amounts, and submissibility of punitive liability.

headings.title: Second stage determination of punitive damages amount
headings.reviewNote: Directs the same jury to determine the amount of punitive damages in a second stage of trial if liability was found in the first stage.

headings.title: Post-trial motion for credit for prior punitive awards
headings.reviewNote: Establishes procedures for post-trial motions requesting credits against punitive awards for amounts previously paid in other cases.

headings.title: Inapplicability of punitive credits to intentional tort actions
headings.reviewNote: Excludes intentional tort actions including defamation, assault, battery, false imprisonment, and fraud from punitive damage credits.

headings.title: Application of remittitur and additur to punitive awards
headings.reviewNote: Applies doctrines of judicial remittitur and additur to jury punitive damage awards based on totality of circumstances.

headings.title: Definition of punitive damage award in bifurcated proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Defines punitive damage award to include punitive damages, exemplary damages, or awards for aggravating circumstances.

headings.title: Asset discovery restricted until leave to plead punitive damages is granted
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits discovery regarding a defendant's assets until the court grants leave to file a pleading seeking punitive damages.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 8 subsections and sections 538.305/510.262 cross-references on bifurcated punitive trials, post-trial prior-award credits, intentional tort exclusions, remittitur/additur, and asset discovery.

headings.title: Statutory cap on punitive damages awards
headings.reviewNote: Imposes statutory limits on punitive damage awards to greater of $500,000 or five times net judgment; note flags Lewellen unconstitutionality.

headings.title: Exemption for civil rights discrimination actions under chapter 213
headings.reviewNote: Exempts civil actions under section 213.111 alleging violations of housing-related sections 213.040, 213.045, 213.050, or specified housing provisions of section 213.070.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections, cross-references, and Lewellen v. Franklin (441 S.W.3d 136) annotation; aligned subsection 2 note to housing-related chapter 213 sections.

headings.title: Request for written jury instructions on applicable law
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes parties to request written instructions on the law at the close of evidence and requires instructions to be settled before argument.

headings.title: Marking refused instructions and submission of given instructions to jury
headings.reviewNote: Requires refused instructions to be marked and filed, and mandates that given instructions be carried to the jury room and returned with the verdict.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked both subsections on requests for written jury instructions, court-motion instructions, marking refused instructions, and filing given instructions.

headings.title: Evidentiary rulings and offers of proof in bench trials
headings.reviewNote: Governs court rulings on evidentiary objections in nonjury trials and procedures for preserving excluded testimony and evidence in the record.

headings.title: Judgment rendition and requested findings of fact and conclusions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes rendition of judgment and requires findings on controverted fact issues and grounds of decision when requested before submission.

headings.title: Motion to amend judgment and findings in nonjury trials
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes motions to amend judgments and factual findings within ten days of entry, permitting joinder with motions for new trial.

headings.title: Scope of appellate review in bench trials
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that unrequested findings are unnecessary for review and establishes standards for appellate review of facts and credibility in bench trials.

entries.reviewSummary: Source-checked all 4 subsections on bench-trial evidentiary rulings/offers of proof, requested findings/opinions, 10-day motions to amend, and appellate review.
